<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" /></noinclude><section begin=par152 />{{GHGpar-heading|152|Negative Sentences}}

{{GHGmargin-letter|152|a}}
'''1.''' Besides the use of rhetorical questions ({{GHGpar|150|d|doublesign=1}}, {{GHGpar|151|a|nosign=1}}), independent sentences are made negative by the adverbs {{GHGheb|text=לֹא}} ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=6|verse=21}}, where instead of the {{GHGterm|K<sup>e</sup>th.}} {{GHGheb|text=לוֹ}} we must evidently read {{GHGheb|text=לֹא}}; perhaps preserved as a substantive) = the Greek οὐ, ''not'', {{GHGheb|text=אַל־}} = μή ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=24|verse=25}} as a substantive), {{GHGheb|text=אֵין}} (''it is'') ''not''; {{GHGheb|text=טֶ֫רֶם|translate=not yet}}, {{GHGheb|text=אֶ֫פֶס|translate=not}}, {{GHGheb|text=אַפְסִי}} (cf. {{GHGpar|90|m}}) ''not''. The forms {{GHGheb|text=בַּל}}, {{GHGheb|text=בְּלִי}}, {{GHGheb|text=בִּלְתִּי|translate=not}} belong almost entirely to poetry.—With regard to {{GHGheb|text=לֹא}} and {{GHGheb|text=אֵין}} the main distinction is that verbal-clauses (rarely noun-clauses, see ''e'') are regularly negatived by {{GHGheb|text=לֹא}} (besides its use as negativing ''single'' words<ref>Especially in compounds, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=לֹא־אֵל}} lit. ''a no-God'' (Germ. ''Ungott'') who is indeed called a god, but is not really a god, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=32|verse=21}}; {{GHGheb|text=לֹא אֱלֹהַּ}} verse 17, cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=5|verse=7}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 Ch|chapter=13|verse=9}}; {{GHGheb|text=לֹא־עָם}} lit. ''a not-people'' (Germ. ''Unvolk''), {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=32|verse=21}}; {{GHGheb|text=לֹא דָבָר|translate=a nothing}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Am|chapter=6|verse=13}}; {{GHGheb|text=לֹא עֵץ}} lit. ''not-wood'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=10|verse=15}}; {{GHGheb|text=לֹא־אִישׁ}}, {{GHGheb|text=לֹֽא־אָדָם}} lit. ''not-man'', ''superhuman'' (of God), {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=31|verse=8}}; {{GHGheb|text=לֹא־צֶ֫דֶק|translate=unrighteousness}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=22|verse=13}}, cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=22|verse=29}}; {{GHGheb|text=לֹא־סְדָרִים|translate=disorder}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=10|verse=22}}; {{GHGheb|text=לֹֽא־חָמָם|translate=not-violence}}, 16:17; after {{GHGheb|text=לְ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=26|verse=2}} f. ({{GHGheb|text=לֹא־כֹחַ}}, {{GHGheb|text=לֹא־עֹז|translate=helplessness}}, {{GHGheb|text=לֹא חָכְמָה|translate=insipientia}}); cf. also {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=55|verse=2}} {{GHGheb|text=בְּלוֹא לְשָׂבְעָה|translate=for what is unsatisfying}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=44|verse=13}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=8|verse=11}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=15|verse=32|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 Ch|chapter=12|verse=33}}.—In {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=20|verse=5}} a construct state with several genitives is negatived by {{GHGheb|text=לֹא}}.—Also {{GHGheb|text=לֹא}} is used with an infinitive, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=35|verse=23}}; with an adjective, {{GHGheb|text=לֹא חָכָם|translate=unwise}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=32|verse=6}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ho|chapter=13|verse=13}}; {{GHGheb|text=לֹֽא־חָסִיד|translate=impius}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=43|verse=1}}; {{GHGheb|text=לֹא־עָז}} and {{GHGheb|text=לֹֽא־עָצוּם|translate=not strong}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=30|verse=25}} f.; {{GHGheb|text=לֹא־כֵן|translate=unsuitably}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=7|verse=9}}; {{GHGheb|text=לֹא־טוֹב|translate=not-good}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=65|verse=2}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=20|verse=25}}, &c.; {{GHGheb|text=לֹא טָהוֹר|translate=not-clean}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 Ch|chapter=30|verse=17}}; with a participle, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=2|verse=2}} (''unsown''); 6:8, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=4|verse=14}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=22|verse=24|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Zp|chapter=2|verse=1}}, 3:5; the Masora, however, requires {{GHGheb|text=נֻחָ֫מָה}} in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=54|verse=11}}, {{GHGheb|text=נֶֽעֱזָ֫בָה}} in 62:12, {{GHGheb|text=נוֹשָׁ֫בָה}} in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=6|verse=8}}, {{GHGheb|text=רֻחָ֫מָה}} in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ho|chapter=1|verse=6}}, i.e. always 3rd sing. fem. perf. in pause = ''she was not comforted'', &c., and consequently not compounds, but either relative clauses or ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=54|verse=11}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ho|chapter=1|verse=6}}, and especially 2:25) main clauses instead of proper names.—On the above compounds generally, cf. the dissertation mentioned in {{GHGpar|81|d}}, note 2; on their use in sentences expressing a state, to convey attributive ideas, see ''u'' below.</ref>), while {{GHGheb|text=אֵין}} is used exclusively with noun-clauses (see the examples below).

{{GHGmargin-letter|152|b}}
The conjunctions {{GHGheb|text=פֶּן־}} and {{GHGheb|text=לְבִלְתִּי|translate=that not}}, serve to negative dependent clauses. The particular uses of these particles are as follows:—

(''a'') {{GHGheb|text=לֹא}} (less frequently {{GHGheb|text=לוֹא}}), like οὐ, οὐκ, is used regularly for the ''objective, unconditional'' negation, and hence is usually connected with the perfect or imperfect (as indicative); on {{GHGheb|text=לֹא}} with the imperfect to express an unconditional prohibition, see {{GHGpar|107|o}}; on its use with the jussive, see {{GHGpar|109|d}}.—On {{GHGheb|text=לֹא}} for {{GHGheb|text=הֲלֹא|translate=nonne}}, in interrogative sentences, cf. {{GHGpar|150|a}}. In connexion with {{GHGheb|text=כֹּל}}, {{GHGheb|text=כָּל־}} (= ''any''), {{GHGheb|text=לֹא}} is used to express an ''absolute'' negation, ''nullus, none whatever'' (cf. the French ''ne... personne, ne... rien''), usually in the order {{GHGheb|text=לֹא... כֹּל}}, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=3|verse=1}} {{GHGheb|text=לֹא תֹֽאכְלוּ מִכֹּל עֵץ הַגָּן|translate=ye shall not eat of any tree of the garden}}; 9:11, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=10|verse=15}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=20|verse=10|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=7|verse=23}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=8|verse=9}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=13|verse=7}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=32|verse=17|hidebook=1}} ({{GHGheb|text=לֹא... כָּל־דָּבָר|translate=nothing at all}}; cf. the same statement in the form of a rhetorical question, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=32|verse=27}}); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=12|verse=21}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=30|verse=30|hidebook=1}}<section end=par152 /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>
